text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The Punjab provincial parliament unanimously adopted a resolution calling upon the federal government to review all power purchase agreements signed by the previous government with independent power plants.
- The government has decided to make it compulsory on all telephone subscribers, cars and house owners to file income tax and wealth tax returns from the next financial year.
- Three activists of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and two belonging to its breakaway Haqiqi faction were shot dead in three separate incidents of violence in Karachi.
- A meeting chaired by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif decided not to reduce defence spending in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has allowed non-banking financial institutions to place with it listed term finance certificates apart from government securities for statutory liquidity requirement.
- The government is likely to freeze wages of government employees for one year in the forthcoming federal busget due on Friday to contain expenditure and inflation.

- The government of Pakistan and Turkmenistan in a joint decision have nominated U.S.-based Unocal Corp as leader of a consortium to undertake a $2.5 billion gas pipeline project to bring natural gas from Turkmenistan to Pakistan via Afghanistan.
- The Privatisation Commission meets on Wednesday to hold bidding for Habib Credit and Exchange Bank and appoint U.S.-based Citibank as financial advisor for the sale of Habib Bank Ltd.
- The World Bank will provide $187 million to develop Karachi Port, the federal secretary of communications said.
- The private Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said about a million tonnes of unsold sugar was in stock with mills.
THE MUSLIM
- The accountability cell at the prime minister's secretariat has completed investigation into 35 cases of corruption against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto and her spouse Asif Ali Zardari.
- Ghinwa Bhutto, widow of Murtaza Bhutto, said the inquiry tribunal has exonerated only President Farooq Leghari in the murder of her husband.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has been accorded status of opposition leader in the National Assembly.
THE NEWS
- The government is considering a proposal to introduce massive tariff reforms to support export-oriented industries.
- Lawyers will observe a countrywide strike today to protest against the murder of Ghulam Mustafa Jafery, an advocate.
THE NATION
- The Pakistan People's Party denied allegations of corruption levelled against Asif Ali Zardari by Senator Saif ur Rehman, chief of the prime minister's accountability cell.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
